sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No.11968/2024, which is first application under Section 389 (1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant - Nilesh.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted by Additional Sessions Judge, Chaurai, District Chhindwara in Special Case No.06/2022 vide judgment dated 24.04.2024 for the offences under Sections 363, 366 and 376(2)(n) of IPC read with Section 5(1)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years with fine of Rs.500/-, R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1000/- and life imprisonment with fine of Rs.2,000/- respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Chaurai, District Chhindwara
entities.label: COURT

sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The prosecution story found to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is that in Village Titari, Police Station Chand, District Chhindwara on 20.06.2022 at about 04:00 PM the appellant kidnapped the prosecutrix from the lawful guardianship of her parents and took her to District Chandrapur and committed sexual intercourse with her repeatedly without her consent and will.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: On this finding 2 CRA-5991-2024 the appellant has been convicted and sentenced for the offence, as mentioned above.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that he has been falsely implicated in the case.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. has deposed that she went along with the appellant on her own volition and stay with him in Nagpur for around one month.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: During that period physical relationship was also established between them.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: On 20.07.2022, they married in a temple in Seoni.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: In her Court statement also the prosecturix has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution case.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: As per medical report Ex.-P/21 there is no external or internal injuries were found on the private part of the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The DNA has not been conducted.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The age of the prosecutrix was more than 17 years of age at the time of incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The appellant has already suffered more than 1 1/2 years of incarceration.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: This appeal is of the year 2024 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned Deputy Advocate General for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and submitted that looking to the age of the prosecutrix and the nature of allegations made against the appellant, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the Court statement, it appears to be a case of consensual sexual relationship, therefore, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

sentences._hearing_file: Nilesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025.json

opennyai_summary.14_June_2024__facts:
The petitioner has been arrested 13.04.2024 by Police Station Baheriya District Sagar in connection with Crime No.148/2024 registered in relation to offences punishable u/Ss. 366, 376 (D), 506 of the IPC.
Petitioner is alleged with gang rape along with other co-accused persons.
opennyai_summary.14_June_2024__decision:
It would be appropriate that the victim is allowed to be examined in the Court before request for bail is cancelled or if the trial gets further delayed whichever is earlier.

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Shri Gopal Singh Baghel- learned counsel and Shri Vikes  Singh- learned counsel for the appellant.
Ms. Shweta Yadav- Deputy Advocate   respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No.11968/2024, which is first application under Section 389 (1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant - Nilesh.
opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.
On 20.07.2022, they married in a temple in Seoni.
In her Court statement also the prosecturix has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution case.
As per medical report Ex.-P/21 there is no external or internal injuries were found on the private part of the prosecutrix.
The DNA has not been conducted.
The age of the prosecutrix was more than 17 years of age at the time of incident.
The appellant has already suffered more than 1 1/2 years of incarceration.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the Court statement, it appears to be a case of consensual sexual relationship, therefore, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Accordingly, I.A. No.11968/2024, is allowed.
It is directed that substantive jail sentence of appellant - Nilesh shall remain suspended subject to his depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on 28.04.2025 and on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Court concerned in this behalf.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
